independence_declaration.statement: I am code-security-reviewer, session b5b4d929-9047-48b6-99d7-f47da960b43d, task T-DG7-REV-CS-RG1. I verified the assignment's sha256 (b960757eb5d5015e0c993f641489e47a024a7a8de619117237c02c402267340b), and I authored no implementation in the DG7 scope. P7 and its repairs were built by solution-architect, backend-workflow-engineer, kpi-benefits-engineer, frontend-ux-engineer, devops-engineer and transformation-analyst; qa-verifier wrote the pre-freeze acceptance tests, and delivery-orchestrator integrated the work and ran the drills. I formed this verdict without reading any other reviewer's round-1 record or evidence. The directories docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/{domain,qa}/round-1 existed during my run, and I did not open them. Two inconsistencies in the assignment are reported, not followed. It asks for `round: 7`, but the record path is round-1 and tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs l.682/794 requires rec.round to equal the round directory and the stages.json round entry (round 1), so this record says round 1. This review is engineering evidence only: it grants no business, Finance or IT approval, product gate G6 does not imply DG7, and DG7 implies no G1-G6 approval.

checks_run.procedure: Read the configuration-bundle routes, service, plan and every kind adapter, and check authorization, validation, optimistic concurrency, locking, audit, the per-kind right (ADR-0065 §8), no publish, and the explicit refusal of unportable kinds (ADR-0065 Amendment 1).
checks_run.command: git diff 944aaf810..ddf42ccd2 plus the full files: apps/api/src/modules/transfer/config-bundle/{routes,service,plan,registry}.ts, apps/api/src/modules/{admin/config-bundle-adapters,jobs/config-bundle-adapter,methodology/config-bundle-adapter,tasks/config-bundle-adapter}.ts
checks_run.expected: Every operation checks config_bundle.* at the row's organization. Mutations re-check rights inside the transaction, use If-Match plus the organization lock plus FOR UPDATE, and write an audit event. A commit re-plans and never widens a user's rights, and never publishes.
checks_run.actual: As expected. requireSomeRight and requireRightAt guard every route. freshRightAt (service.ts l.404) re-checks on reloaded grants inside the transaction. Validate and commit take the configBundleImport lock, lock the row FOR UPDATE and check the version. The stored object is read outside the transaction and checked against its SHA-256. plan.ts refuses kind_not_permitted with the reloaded principal, and each adapter re-checks the kind's right at write time with that kind's own rules: upload_policy and branding apply as their routes do; job schedules are written disabled with an outbox event; methodology kinds are written as drafts only, under lockConfigDraft; review policies refuse AUD and technical_admin reviewers. Unportable kinds are refused with 422, never dropped. No finding.

checks_run.procedure: Read the migration export API, the export plan and manifest, the owner-role import, attachment copy-in, path confinement, identity rebind and unbound sign-in. Sweep the final schema for credential-like columns that the exclusion rules do not cover.
checks_run.command: Source review of apps/api/src/modules/transfer/**, packages/db/src/transfer/{plan,manifest,export,import,rebind}.ts, packages/db/migrations/0133_p7_transfer_migration_manifest.sql, apps/api/src/modules/identity/{oidc,routes}.ts; awk sweep of packages/db/src/schema.ts for hash|token|secret|password|key|credential|nonce|verifier column names
checks_run.expected: No row data or credential leaves through the API. The import loads into an empty database only, never disables or edits audit_event, and is free of SQL injection and path traversal. Unbound carried users cannot sign in.
checks_run.actual: As expected; details in 05-static-review-notes.md. The export needs migration.export at organization scope; it is installation-wide by design (ADR-0064 §7, Residual 4). Manifests are served only when succeeded and checksum-matched, and hold no row values. session and oidc_login_state are excluded, and every *_ref secret reference is unbound. The import verifies that the audit_event triggers are enabled, disables only the user triggers of the other tables inside one transaction, compares the table and column sets with the target catalogue, quotes identifiers and binds row values as one JSON parameter. confinedPath refuses absolute paths and '..'. Both OIDC and dev login refuse identity_unbound. The schema sweep found no unclassified credential. Observation: automation_rule_version.restricted_token_key (0127, a per-row HMAC key for restricted tokens) travels in the package as row data so that tokens stay valid after transfer; it is not a password hash, session or credential, so the REQ-S19-016 'no password hashes' clause holds. No finding.

summary:
FAIL, with two Medium findings that must be repaired before the gate (D-192) and one Low documentation finding.
- F-DG7-1011 (Medium, REQ-S16-031): secret-scan.mjs l.89 exempts every lower-case alphanumeric S3 value as an 'i18n key' before the entropy rule. A committed 48-hex password (init-secrets.sh's own `openssl rand -hex 24` shape) therefore passes the repository scan, contrary to ADR-0063 §5 and security-controls.md SC-13. Probes show nothing is hidden today.
- F-DG7-1012 (Medium, REQ-S19-012): backup.sh writes the full database dump (users, audit, sessions) as 0644 in 0755 directories, and the Compose backup profile falls back to the host's /tmp/mth-backups.
- F-DG7-1013 (Low, REQ-S02-005): ADR-0071 §5.1-§5.2 not amended for the release-notes disclosures input and section (D-280; the old F-DG7-973 raised afresh).
Everything else I reviewed in P7 is sound: configuration bundles, migration export and import, retention and purge, the OIDC loopback exception, the scanner allow-lists, the image and Compose changes, and seal and verify. The candidate identity holds (sha256:9822d8fe, 3158 files), --historical DG6-DG1 and --pipeline pass, register DG7 passes, the P7 integration suites pass (322/322) and so do the unit suites (608/608). The release-tool suite passes, except for failures explained by the sparse clone (T-H4, which then passes 51/51) and by this sandbox (T-A5). The real-build asset scan (T-A5/T-A11) is BLOCKED here: the HOME pnpm store is read-only and lacks the @aws-sdk/client-s3 tarball. REQ-DLV-030's progress.md clause is not demonstrated (A27 K11 partial); per D-274 the acceptance decision is the release-auditor's. The record's round is 1, not the assignment's 7, as the validator requires.
